cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven cotton hunter's/warrior's tunic with sewn amulets containing Arabic texts and small horns attached, a well-documented West African hunter's garment type consistent with Kissi/Guinea region material culture.

physical.title: tunic; shirt
physical.summary: Hunter's or warrior's tunic: composed of 14 strips of  hand-spun and hand-woven cotton. Plain woven with brown warps and wefts which are hemmed around the neck and bottom of the tunic. The tunic is square in shape with an oval shaped neck and two holes for the arms (no sleeves). In the central narrow strip on both front and back there are three amulets (probably containing Arabic texts) wrapped in cotton. There are also two small horns sewn to the back of the neck. At the bottom of the neck on the inside of the tunic there is a large 'pocket'. Inside the pocket there is a large circular protective device composed of vegetable matter.
